about: Australian Road Rules (Victoria) audit of sim/net/roads.net.xml and the SUMO behaviour. Evidence from network queries and TraCI micro-scenarios.

rules.rule: Give way to the right at uncontrolled cross intersections (ARR r.72)
rules.network: 47 left_before_right junctions (--junctions.left-before-right, plus right_of_way.nod.xml for unsigned cross intersections of equal minor streets at 50 km/h, where netconvert's 49 km/h threshold had made them priority junctions)
rules.how: SUMO's left-hand mode mirrors its default right_before_left into give way to the LEFT (tested: the westbound car stopped for one coming from its left). left_before_right in a left-hand network gives way to the right.

rules.rule: T-intersections: the terminating road gives way (ARR r.69)
rules.network: the terminating road's edges get a lower priority than the continuing road's (sim/patches/net/t_intersections.edg.xml), and equal-priority T-junctions become priority junctions (right_of_way.nod.xml)

evidence.roundabout_note: at these OSM junction=roundabout nodes the entering road gives way to the circulating one (r.114 overrides r.69), although the entry lines up with the exit

rules.how: netconvert broke ties between equal-class streets by speed, so an untagged 50 km/h side street beat a continuing street signed 40 km/h: 69 of 311 judged T-intersections were backwards before

rules.rule: Give-way and stop signs (ARR r.67-69); stop means stop
rules.network: OSM highway=give_way / stop nodes mapped to the approach they sign; junctions with a stop-signed approach are priority_stop (SUMO does not import stop signs)
rules.how: stop-signed priority junctions became priority_stop (vehicles stop), and signed roads were given a lower edge priority than the others at their junction (sim/patches/net/right_of_way.nod.xml, give_way_priorities.edg.xml)
rules.note: approaches_with_priority are signed approaches whose movement still has priority over a conflicting one (equal-priority geometry netconvert resolves by straightness); 'no conflicting traffic' approaches have nothing to give way to

rules.rule: Roundabouts: give way to vehicles already in the roundabout (ARR r.114)
Keep left unless overtaking; overtake on the right (ARR r.129-130, 141)
rules.network: SUMO LC2013 lane changing; in a left-hand network lane 0 is the left lane and its keep-right tendency (lcKeepRight) keeps cars to lane 0

evidence.lane_index_note: lane 0 is the left (kerb) lane in a left-hand network

rules.rule: Speed limits: signed maxspeed; 50 km/h default in built-up areas (ARR r.20, 25)
rules.network: OSM maxspeed where tagged; untagged non-motorway roads 50 km/h (sim/patches/osm/urban_speed_defaults.typ.xml), 40 km/h inside the Hoddle Grid (CBD area limit), shared zones 10 km/h
rules.note: cbd_edges_above_50 are OSM-tagged 60 km/h arterials on the CBD fringe (Dudley St, Batman Ave and their ramps), listed for review. cbd_area_limit_40: untagged roads inside the Hoddle Grid get the CBD 40 km/h area limit (sim/patches/net/cbd_speed_limit.edg.xml); untagged_cbd_box_edges_left_at_50 lie in the wider CBD_BOX but outside the grid (north of La Trobe St, Docklands, south of Flinders St), where the area limit is not established and nearby ways are tagged 50

rules.rule: No turning on a red light (ARR r.56-57; Australia has no general turn-on-red)
rules.network: SUMO default static signal programs (90 s placeholders)

evidence.arrow_note: a right-turn (or U-turn) green while the shared lane's through movement is red is a protected turn arrow phase, which Australian signals use; allowed

rules.how: with no pedestrians simulated, netconvert's default programs left kerb-side left turns green in every phase (a left turn on red); the build now makes each left turn follow its approach's through movement (sim/generated_patches.py no_left_turn_on_red; the build log prints how many links it changed: 58 in 48 programs)
rules.note: uncontrolled_links_at_signals are slip lanes and bays that netconvert left outside the signal ('o': give way, as at a slip lane with a give-way sign). Opposing right turns green together pass in front of each other in left-hand traffic: see opposing_right_turns

opposing_right_turns.verdict_note: compliant: opposing right turns green together pass in front of each other; where their paths do cross, both are permissive green ('g'), so SUMO makes them give way to each other

rules.rule: Bus lanes: only buses may drive in them (ARR r.154-158)
rules.network: bus lanes from the extract's lane access tags (bus:lanes, lanes:bus, busway) closed to cars with --osm.lane-access (sim/bus_lanes.py)

always_on_listed_without_hours.label: full-time: the City of Melbourne lists it with no hours, and Transport Victoria's rule is that a bus-lane sign with no times operates 24/7 (https://transport.vic.gov.au/road-and-active-transport/road-rules-and-safety/driving-with-buses/driving-with-buses-video-transcript)

rules.verdict: fixed (timed lanes per scenario clock; others full-time)
rules.how: counted (lanes:bus) and busway=lane bus lanes are placed on the kerb lane, where Victorian bus lanes run (r.158 lets cars cross into one to turn left); explicit bus:lanes values and sides are used as tagged. netconvert builds the junction connections with the bus lanes in place, so cars turn from the lanes they may use (movements_only_buses_can_make is empty). Hours (sim/bus_lane_hours.py): the City of Melbourne bus-lanes page gives part-time hours for Queen St east side (Mo-Fr 16:30-18:30), Lonsdale St north side (Mo-Fr 16:00-18:30), Lonsdale St south side (Mo-Fr 07:00-09:30) and City Rd inbound (Mo-Fr 06:30-10:00); those lanes are matched by street name, side (geometry) and cross streets, carry a busLaneHours lane param, and are OPEN to cars in this baseline network (no clock time). A scenario with a clock closes them in their hours (bus_lane_hours.bus_only_lanes). See evidence.hours for the lanes

assumptions: kerb-lane placement of counted bus lanes (OSM gives only the count)
OSM has no bus-lane hours (no :conditional tags); hours come from the City of Melbourne page (https://www.melbourne.vic.gov.au/bus-lanes), used as cited facts with George's approval (2026-10-27)
timed lanes assume an ordinary weekday (public holidays unknown to a scenario)
only the OSM-tagged part of each listed stretch is a bus lane in the network (e.g. City Rd: 2 short one-way edges; its two-way ways do not say which direction has the bus lane and are skipped)
rules.not_modelled: cars entering a bus lane for up to 100 m to turn (r.158(2)); buses themselves (cars only)

rules.network: signed limits only; conditional limits apply per scenario clock (sim/conditional_speeds.py)

evidence.why_not_baseline: the baseline scenario is placeholder demand in simulation seconds with no time of day or weekday, so no window can contain it; the signed limits stay
evidence.phase3_am_peak: apply with sim.conditional_speeds.edge_speeds(osm, idx, start time) when the scenario has a clock: on a school weekday the Dudley St school zone (40 km/h) runs 08:00-09:30 and Bay St / Crockford St (40 km/h) from 08:00, so a 07:00-09:00 AM peak would switch them on at 08:00

rules.verdict: not applied to baseline (no time of day); ready for the Phase 3 AM peak

rules.rule: Shared zones: 10 km/h unless signed lower, give way to pedestrians (ARR r.24, r.83)
rules.impact: no pedestrians are simulated, so cars never yield to them in shared zones; they only drive at 10 km/h

cannot_be_modelled.why: SUMO has no hook-turn manoeuvre; OSM tags no hook-turn intersection here (0 ways, 0 relations).
cannot_be_modelled.impact: at signed CBD intersections cars turn right from the centre lane at the same time as through traffic, instead of waiting in the kerb lane for the cross street's green: right-turn queues and conflicts look different from reality

cannot_be_modelled.why: cars only; no tram vehicles, schedules or tram signals
cannot_be_modelled.impact: cars never queue behind trams, give way to them or stop for passengers at kerbside tram stops (r.163-164); tram-only lanes and tracks are either absent or driven as ordinary lanes (439 tram track ways in the raw data)

cannot_be_modelled.why: no open signal-timing data for Melbourne (SCATS is not published)
cannot_be_modelled.impact: every signal runs SUMO's static 90 s default program; no coordination (green waves), no actuation, no pedestrian-demand phases

cannot_be_modelled.item: Clearways (kerb lanes open only in peak hours)
cannot_be_modelled.why: OSM has no structured clearway or parking-lane-condition tags here (21 ways mention it in free text)
cannot_be_modelled.impact: kerb lanes are always open, as if every clearway were in force (true in the AM peak on most arterials, too generous off-peak)
no give way to pedestrians at turns (r.62, r.72) or crossings, no pedestrian phases beyond the placeholder programs; bike lanes not simulated

cannot_be_modelled.why: cars only (Phase 2 decision); full-time bus lanes are closed to cars (see the bus lane rule) but no bus runs in them
cannot_be_modelled.impact: no bus traffic or stops; bus lanes look empty

known_issues.why: two joined-junction shapes made SUMO route a left turn along a loop inside the junction (Nott St to Princes St, 85.6 m for a 23.4 m gap, through a house; a 49.8 m loop at Batmans Hill Dr, Docklands); both are now kept out of junction joining (build_net.JOIN_EXCLUDE) and this scan (junction lanes > 40 m and > 2.5 x their straight gap) finds none
netconvert moves the ends of edges into a joined junction, so near joined junctions an edge lies a few metres off its OSM line (alignment: share_within_own_way below share_within_any_carriageway)
known_issues.impact: cars near joined junctions are drawn slightly off their OSM centreline

known_issues.item: Elizabeth St at Bourke St: signals on separate stop-line nodes
known_issues.why: OSM's four-node box was not joined, so its three stop-line signals were their own lights and the box gave way to the right; sim/patches/osm/elizabeth_bourke_signals.nod.xml joins and signalises it
netconvert resolves some equal-priority geometries by straightness
